summary: Sticky error detection for command consistency and one-hot encoding violations.
behavior: This continuous region implements sticky error flags for two conditions. The combinational next-state signal cmd_consty_err_d captures a command consistency error: when cmd_chk is asserted and the current enables (enables_q) differ from the expected enables (enables_d), the error is set; otherwise it retains the latched value from cmd_consty_err_q. The signal one_hot_err_d detects a one-hot error: if the bitwise AND of enables_d and enables_sub is non-zero (indicating more than one enable bit is active), the error is set; otherwise it retains one_hot_err_q. Both errors are sticky—once triggered, the _d signals stay high as long as the _q states are fed back, providing a permanent latch unless cleared by external logic (not in this fragment).

guarantees.property: Once a command consistency error is detected, cmd_consty_err_d remains asserted (sticky) until explicitly reset.
Once a one-hot error is detected, one_hot_err_d remains asserted (sticky) until explicitly reset.

security_implications: These sticky error detectors are marked as a security countermeasure (SEC_CM: KMAC_IF_CMD.CTRL.CONSISTENCY). They guard against fault-induced multi-command activation or unexpected command changes. A latched error can be used to block subsequent operations or raise an alarm, preventing safety/security policy violations.

assumptions.constraint: enables_sub must be a mask selecting all enable bits except the currently expected active one, such that a non-zero (enables_d & enables_sub) indicates a multi-enable violation.
assumptions.bug_relevance: If enables_sub is incorrectly defined, one-hot errors may be falsely triggered or missed, compromising the safety mechanism.

assumptions.constraint: enables_q and enables_d must have identical width and represent the same set of enable signals; otherwise the consistency check may produce incorrect results.
assumptions.bug_relevance: Width mismatch or semantic misalignment can cause false/stuck errors or allow undetected command inconsistency.

uncertain_points: The clearing/reset condition for cmd_consty_err_q and one_hot_err_q is not defined in this fragment; it is unclear whether a system reset or a state-machine action clears them.
The exact definition of enables_sub (its bit mapping relative to enables_d) is not provided here; it must be inferred from surrounding logic.
